Also in terms of terms of reference, we would wonder whether the expert, your expert would actually look at and comment upon the reports of the parties' experts, whether your expert would produce a report, and if so, what the schedule would be for our -- for us to respond or for our expert to look at it, and then of course the issue of cross-examination, related to which is -- the question is will this be evidence against the accused? Because if it's in any way going to be evidence against the accused, then of course I submit we have to be able to cross-examine him. And Your Honour has assuaged my concerns about that the other day. But, again, an issue to flag up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Might have assuaged even further, Mr. Jones, apart from what I said last time on the basis of what we had discussed in my room, there is also always the possibility if this arises of both of you or either of you recalling as expert -- your ex parte expert witnesses to give further testimony arising out of the experts -- the court-appointed -- sorry, Trial Chamber-appointed handwriting expert. So please take -- for the time being at least that all options are open and that you will even have, if you require it, the possibility of having the expert sit -- sitting down with you there during the testimony of our expert to help you put questions. And if you want to bring him over to give evidence, again recall him later on, yes, of course, it's -- there is a safeguard in the Rules. Please don't ask me which rule number it is. But while we adhere to the principle that a prospective witness should never be present in the courtroom while another witness is giving evidence, that rule does not apply to a prospective expert, for example, or a court expert. So please feel safe, hundred per cent safe that we will provide you with -- you and the Prosecution with all the opportunities you require to fulfil your obligations towards Prosecution in one case and the accused in the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: To the utmost.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour. I'm very obliged for that. Just in that regard -- in that regard, and again, as I say, I'm just -- really mentioning issues now rather than looking for an immediate response. But there's also, in relation to cross-examination, the issue raised by Mr. Wubben this morning of whether, in fact, we could produce to the court-appointed, the Chamber-appointed expert, documents which he hadn't examined but nonetheless which we wish to show to him for his comment. Again, that would be something which would be important for us because -- especially if the expert has a -- doesn't have a full sample in the end, we may want to show him documents which are experted, looked at to get his or her opinion on that. I come to the issue - I think it's the fourth issue - of non-contentious signatures, and that is a very complex issue for two reasons. The position is -- was correctly summarised by Ms. Sellers in that I think it's P100 is a Prosecution -- I believe Prosecution -- P100 is a collection of signatures allegedly made by our client during the course of his interview and a declaration of Mr. Tedder, and I think someone else goes to that issue, and we didn't insist on the right to cross-examine Mr. Tedder on that, and so those samples we used as non-contentious signatures for the Prosecution expert report. It's not possible to say that, therefore, those signatures are not contentious at all from the Defence side for at least one issue which is -- this is, as I say, where it gets complicated. Very shortly we will be submitting a motion regarding the interview of our client, asking for it to be excluded. Now, if his interview is excluded, then the signatures which were taken during the course of his interview for the reasons mentioned in the -- in our motion may be the fruits of a poison tree to use -- I think it's an American phrase, although it's sometimes used in the UK as well. And so that's why we can't simply say that it's -- that there is no dispute concerning those signatures. There is a dispute of sorts. And as for the others used by our expert, Professor Bilic, non-contentious samples, not just of the accused but also of Hamed Salihovic and Hamdija Fejzic, they haven't been disclosed or filed, and we would have to very seriously consider the position of providing, as Your Honour appreciates, samples of our client's signature. That's an extremely, seriously important matter which we would have to consider. The fifth point which I've just marked down is whether the -- any report produced by the court-appointed -- Chamber-appointed expert would be evidence in this case, but that's -- in a way, I've touched on that already. And just the final concern I have is sort of a philosophical one, if I may put it that way, which is this: That the expert that we selected, we are putting forward, is an independent expert, and the Prosecution in the same spirit put forward an independent expert. So firstly just in terms of terminology, I suppose, we wouldn't want there to be a suggestion that there is the independent expert and then the parties' experts so that whatever the Chamber-appointed expert says would have a greater value or credibility than the parties' experts. Because, in fact, in our submission the position remains the same, that the expert is not going to be more credible simply because he was appointed by the Trial Chamber. Again, it's a question of weighing how they appear on the stand, their techniques, their methodology, and those sorts of matters. And we would have a concern that if the Chamber-appointed expert only saw, let's say, a few exhibits, let's say he didn't look at the Hamed Salihovic documents, that he would reach a different conclusion from our expert or from the Prosecution expert, that therefore his expertise is taken in preference to our experts and then our experts' conclusions on other matters are discredited by that token. I think Your Honour probably follows the point I'm making. That's something which we're concerned about. Of course, I appreciate that Your Honours will not automatically accept the testimony of your expert in deference to -- I mean, over the parties' experts. So it was simply because Your Honour said that since you, the Chamber, doesn't understand the forensic science of graphology that therefore it was necessary to appoint an expert. But in my submission, the problem remains the same. In any case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are appointing an expert not only because we don't understand the principles or the science of graphology, but mainly because we have got two reports that are diametrically opposed, so -- not completely, but almost completely. So at that point in time we feel helpless -- in a helpless position, and we need help. So whether we would accept that help or not, we may end up with appointing someone and finish up with being completely unhappy with his report, or their reports. I don't know. But we'll strive not to. That's the position basically.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Well, thank you, Your Honour. I'm obliged for you hearing those submissions at this point, and I can subsequently develop them, but I just wanted to put them on the record now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, okay. Thank you. So that's the position. All right. Now, I didn't mention all this to start a discussion because, as I said, who we choose and what the terms of reference will be, of course, will -- is our prerogative. Do you wish to make a submission, Ms. Sellers, or do you wish to postpone it until Mr. Wubben's here?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would just like to make a very brief comment and then ask could we address this tomorrow morning when I can more fully discuss this with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, that's why I'm offering you --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. In terms of an independent forensics expert, I agree with the Defence that I think all the experts are independent. I don't think we have any controversy over the submission of that argument. In terms of the nationality of an expert, of course I think we leave that within the Trial Chamber's hands. I am certain that the Defence has already raised a question concerning the nationality of our expert. We have not chosen at this point and do not anticipate raising questions of bias as related to the nationality of the Defence expert, and we would just ask that the Trial Chamber, in their seeking of terms of reference, go to the crux of the issue, which is the handwriting and, in our opinion, not the nationality. The issue of the person, the expert, having to be familiar with Cyrillic script, being familiar with Latin script, understanding the language, might in some ways limit the experts that one can seek out, and we're aware of that. There are several countries that do use Cyrillic scripts or whatever, but I do not think at this time period that we would want to be hemmed and hawed into choosing one nationality, a type of expert. We are much more concerned with the expertise and just proceeding with the matter. We are going to have other submissions probably concerning Hamed Salihovic and other documents, and I would just like to underscore that at this point in time, prior to the Defence filing their application on the interview, that the only uncontested controlled copies of signatures we have are that as we have agreed in P100.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So I thank you. We will adjourn until tomorrow morning with this proviso. I don't think how our witness is -- will be feeling tomorrow morning. And if she is not a hundred per cent fit to continue giving evidence, I will adjourn; there is no question about it. I will not force her to answer one single question. Same thing applies to you, Madam Vidovic. Should at any time you require an adjournment, please let us know and we will accommodate you for sure. There's no question. I mean, we are, of course, pressed for time, but a day here and a day there is not going to change anything. All right. The only thing is that if there is a shifting of our schedule by one day involving us to sit on the 27th, then we will not be sitting on the 27th because one of them -- one of us has a problem on that day. So we were scheduled to stop on the 26th, or finish on the 26th, but if we don't, then we continue and skip the 27th. All right. Clear enough? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 19th day of January, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.30 p.m.,
